_readme: One entry per mod. The build makes one jar per entry (build/mods/), the mods spreadsheet is made from this file (tools/mods_sheet.py), and 'include' says which code and files go in each jar.

mods.name: Ahrivaea Creatures
mods.summary: 205 creatures (278 forms) that replace every vanilla mob, with drops, Fire Emblem-style grid battles in biome arenas, recruiting, Palworld-style bases where they work, riding (saddle any medium or bigger creature; fliers fly and swimmers swim), and your own levelled-up character.
features: Starter: a new player picks any Common creature (no influence) from a screen with its stats and model when they first join; it joins their party at level 1 (/starter until they've picked)

All 205 creatures from the creature list (278 influence forms), each with its own biomes, rarity, levels, drops and jobs; real models (animated, at their real size) for 275 of the 278 forms: every Arcane, Darkness, Earth, Fae, Fire, Frost, Nature, Radiant, Storm, Void and Water creature and 56 of the 58 None ones. The None Orca uses the Water Orca's model and the Arcane Dragon the None Dragon's until theirs arrive; the Whale is still the placeholder (a block tinted by its influence) until its model arrives

Wild creatures are rare and appear as you explore: about one per 50 blocks travelled (20 on a 1000 block journey, game rule ahrivaea:wild_spawn_distance), one every 90 seconds if you stay put, at most 5 near you; on land, in water, in caves, the Nether and the End, by biome; they never attack first and can't be hurt outside battle
Anti-stuck: a creature inside blocks for 2 seconds, or trying to walk for 6 seconds without moving, hops to the nearest open spot on solid ground within 12 blocks
Influence tiers: None is the most common spawn (44%), then Fire, Water, Nature, Storm, Earth and Frost (33%), then Darkness, Void, Radiant, Fae and Arcane (22%)
Enraged and Mutated creatures: 1 in 10,000 wild creatures, in their own colours and named for it (game rule ahrivaea:variant_odds); they stay that way when caught

No vanilla mobs: natural spawning is off and any vanilla mob that appears is replaced by a creature (a cow becomes a Cow); the Ender Dragon counts as defeated; /gamerule ahrivaea:vanilla_mobs true turns this off

Grid battles seen from above: hit a wild creature with a sword (the only way to start one; they never attack first, and can't be hurt outside battle) and you're taken to your own battle arena built for that biome (25 themes, 15×15 to 27×27, at the world's time of day) to fight it plus its reinforcements (up to 1 at levels 1-10, 2 at 11-20 ... 5 at 41-50, more likely the higher it is); you and 4 of your creatures (the ones you have out first, then your party) each move by Speed, then attack, use an item, rally or wait; afterwards you're brought back to safe ground where you were. The arenas can't be visited outside a battle
Battle screen: drag to look around and scroll to zoom (towards the mouse), team cards on both sides, a turn banner, an action menu beside the unit, floating damage numbers and a results panel
You win by beating every enemy and lose only if you're knocked out yourself. The creature you challenged is gone for good only if you win; otherwise it's back where it was afterwards
Counterattacks, high ground, water and lava, influence matchups, crits and dodges (Luck), support (Charisma), fleeing at any time (always works); the enemy side plays itself

Win XP for yourself and the same for your creatures (they level on the same curve as you, so at your pace), and the defeated creatures' drops. Recruit any defeated creature if you have the creature XP: 100 per level times 1 (Common) to 5 (Legendary), e.g. 400 for a Lv.4 Common. Reinforcements that join a wild creature are never rarer or higher level than it

Bases: a Base Core (5 levels, radius 24-40, 5-15 workers) where assigned creatures work on their own: farming, growth, logging, mining at a Mining Post, smelting and brewing without fuel, carrying items to chests, ranching, fishing, enchanting, powering a Creature Dynamo, running crafters, making ice and putting up torches

Base raids at night (while you're nearby): aggressive creatures attack, Defense workers fight them in real time, raiders that reach the core steal from your chests; knocked-out workers rest instead of dying; /gamerule ahrivaea:base_raids
Your character levels up to 50 and you spend stat points (/character); your weapon and armor count in battle

Riding: put a saddle on your own medium or bigger creature (220 of the 278 forms) and right-click to ride it. Flying creatures take off when you jump and fly where you look (they land softly); swimming creatures swim where you look underwater and keep you breathing; walkers climb full blocks and jump

Mount speed works like Swift Horses: top speed comes from the creature's Speed stat at its level, times its tier (x1.5 to x2.8). Tiers 1-3 from treats (8 Swift Treats, 8 Golden Treats, 4 Racing Treats); tiers 4 and 5 from Speed (60 and 80) once it's at tier 3. Training and saddle stay with it in your party; while riding, its speed, tier and next step show in the corner

Your party on screen: a small summary in the top-left corner (each creature's name, level and HP, plus the ones you've sent out), and a party screen on K (rebindable in Controls) with each creature's HP, XP, all seven stats now and at level 50, jobs and riding, and buttons to send it out, level it up with your XP, move it to or from the box, call it back or release it. The summary can be turned off from the screen

Healing: outside battle your creatures eat food (right-click one you have out, or Feed on the party screen / /party feed <slot> for party creatures), healing more for more filling food (a steak 36%, bread 20%, an apple 13%). In battle only brewed potions heal: Healing 40%, Healing II 70%, Regeneration 30-50%; splash and lingering ones heal neighbours too

Creature dex (J, or Dex on the party screen): every form numbered; unknown ones show a clue to where they live, seen ones their name, model, rarity, levels and habitat, caught ones everything (stats, jobs, drops)
Model import from Blockbench: tools/import_models.py turns Mythic Mob Library .bbmodel files (zipped or not) into the creature's model, idle/fly animations and textures, and sizes its hitbox to match
mods.commands: /starter, /party, /party send|release <slot>, /party recall [entity], /party feed <slot>, /party xp <slot> <amount>, /party box [take <n>|store <slot>], /character, /character spend <stat> <points>; operators: /ahrivaea spawn|givexp|selftest, /battle start|end|recruit, /battle arena <theme>, /battle home, /character givexp, /gamerule ahrivaea:vanilla_mobs, /gamerule ahrivaea:base_raids, /gamerule ahrivaea:wild_spawn_distance, /gamerule ahrivaea:variant_odds, /base raid
mods.players_install: Yes (creatures, models, items, blocks and screens)
mods.status: Creature list phases 1 and 2 done (creatures, drops, bases with every job, raids, no vanilla mobs); real models for every creature but the Whale; Enraged and Mutated variants; placeholder moves; riding (placeholder treat textures; the saddle isn't drawn on the model yet)
guide: Creatures live everywhere instead of the usual Minecraft mobs. They never attack you first.
New here? Pick your starter creature when you first join (or type /starter). It joins your party at level 1.

Start a battle by hitting a wild creature with any sword. You're taken to an arena built for that biome, then brought back to where you were afterwards. Drag to look around the battlefield and scroll to zoom.
In battle, click one of your units, click a square to move, then attack, use an item, rally or wait. Press End turn when you're done. Flee leaves the battle at any time.

Winning gives XP and the creatures' drops. You can recruit any creature you beat if you have the creature XP (100 per level, more for rarer ones). Your creatures earn the same XP you do. A Vessel on a weakened wild creature can catch it too.

Heal your creatures with food outside battle: right-click one you have out, or press Feed on the party screen with food in your hand. In battle only brewed potions (Healing, Regeneration) heal; use them with Item.
Press J for the creature dex: what you've seen and caught, with clues to where the others live.

Your party shows in the top-left corner of the screen. Press K (change it in Controls) for the party screen: stats, XP, riding, and buttons to send creatures out, level them up, call them back or use the box.
/party shows your party (up to 6). Extra creatures go to your box: /party box. /character shows your own level; spend points with /character spend.

Bases: craft a Base Core and place it. Right-click it to put party or box creatures to work. Each works by its job: farming, logging, mining (place a Mining Post), smelting, brewing, enchanting, fishing, ranching and more. Put chests near the core for what they make.
Upgrade a base by right-clicking its core while holding 4 iron blocks, then 4 gold blocks, 2 diamond blocks and 4 emerald blocks. Each level reaches farther and takes more workers.
At night your base may be raided. Creatures with the Defense job fight back, and you can help with a sword. Raiders who reach the core steal from nearby chests.

Riding: right-click your own medium or bigger creature with a saddle, then right-click it to get on. Fliers: jump to take off, look where you want to go. Swimmers dive where you look. Shears take the saddle off.
Make a mount faster with treats: 8 Swift Treats for tier 1, 8 Golden Treats for tier 2, 4 Racing Treats for tier 3. Fast creatures (Speed 60 and 80, which grows with level) go on to tiers 4 and 5.

mods.name: Ahrivaea Tower Challenges
mods.summary: A ruined tower over every stronghold that the whole server rebuilds by donating items, with leaderboards and rewards.
features: A tower generates above the End portal of all 128 strongholds, in blocks that match its biome
Each tower has its own challenge (what to bring and how much) and its own rewards, harder and richer farther from spawn
Offering chest; the tower rebuilds in 4 stages; fireworks and rewards for the top donors when finished
Per-tower leaderboards

Protected land: nobody can break, place or use blocks within 64 blocks of a tower (from 8 below its base up to the sky, so the stronghold stays open) until it's rebuilt. The top donor at completion claims it, and from then on only they can build there. The offering chest always works; creative-mode operators aren't affected
Challenges are set in Tower_Challenges.xlsx
mods.players_install: Yes (it's part of the modpack), though it adds no new items or blocks
mods.status: Working (placeholder tower until the real build)
guide: A ruined tower stands over every stronghold. Follow an Eye of Ender to find one.
Each tower asks for its own item. Put it in the tower's offering chest; everyone on the server works together.
The tower rebuilds in four stages as items come in. When it's finished, the top donors get rewards.
/challenge shows the nearest tower's leaderboard and what it needs. /challenge list shows every tower found so far.
Towers and the land 64 blocks around them are protected until they're rebuilt. The top donor claims the finished tower, and only they can build in and around it.

mods.name: Ahrivaea Stellar Gear
mods.summary: Netherite tools and armor upgraded with a nether star into Stellar gear with special powers.
features: Smithing table: nether star + any netherite tool or armor piece = its Stellar version (keeps enchantments)
Pickaxe and shovel mine 3x3; axe fells whole natural trees but never player-placed logs or builds
Hoe tills and harvests-and-replants 3x3; sword heals 20% of the damage it deals
Full Stellar armor set gives flight
Sneak to use the tools one block at a time
guide: At a smithing table, put a nether star in the template slot and a netherite tool or armor piece next to it to make its Stellar version. Enchantments are kept.
Stellar pickaxe and shovel dig 3x3. The axe fells a whole tree. The hoe tills and harvests 3x3. The sword heals you for some of the damage it deals.
Wear the full Stellar armor set to fly.
Sneak to use a Stellar tool on one block at a time.

mods.name: Ahrivaea Swift Horses
mods.summary: Faster vanilla horses, donkeys and mules with their stats on screen, and a way to train them faster still: feed them up three speed tiers, then breed for the top two. Skeleton horses are always top speed.
features: Every horse, donkey, mule, skeleton horse and zombie horse is 1.5x as fast as vanilla (vanilla horses run 5-14 blocks/sec)
Speed tiers 0-5, each multiplying the horse's own speed: x1.5, x1.76, x2.02, x2.28, x2.54, x2.8. The best-bred horses top out near 40 blocks/sec, faster than a Fast Minecart (30)
Tiers 1-3 by feeding a tamed horse: 8 Swift Feed, then 8 Golden Feed, then 4 Racing Feed (crafted from wheat, sugar, apples, golden carrots, golden apples and a rabbit's foot)

Tiers 4-5 only by breeding: a foal takes the better parent's tier, and two parents on the same tier have a 30% chance of a foal one tier higher. Vanilla speed inheritance still applies, so bloodlines matter
Skeleton horses are always at top speed: the best possible bloodline at tier 5 (about 40 blocks/sec), no training needed. Zombie horses can't breed, so they stop at tier 3

See a horse's stats: look at it (up to 16 blocks) for its speed, tier, jump height, health and what its next tier needs; ride it to keep them in the corner with your current speed; they're also beside its inventory screen
Only for Minecraft's own horses, so it suits a vanilla server. On Ahrivaea, creatures are ridden with the same speed tiers through Ahrivaea Creatures (with treats instead of feed)
The stats only show on servers that have Swift Horses; on other servers a player's copy stays off
mods.commands: /horse (while riding: its stats in chat); operators: /horse settier <0-5>
guide: Every horse, donkey and mule is faster than usual. Skeleton horses are always at top speed.
Look at a horse to see its speed, tier and jump height. While riding, its stats stay in the corner of the screen.
Feed a tamed horse 8 Swift Feed for tier 1, then 8 Golden Feed for tier 2, then 4 Racing Feed for tier 3.
Tiers 4 and 5 come from breeding: a foal gets the better parent's tier, and two parents on the same tier may have a foal one tier higher.

mods.name: Ahrivaea Fast Minecarts
mods.summary: Minecarts go up to 30 blocks a second (vanilla: 8), on Minecraft's newer minecart physics so they stay on the rails at speed.
features: Top speed 30 blocks/sec on rails, almost 4x vanilla (half that in water; furnace minecarts go half speed)
Turns on Minecraft's newer minecart physics in every world (normally an experiment you pick when making a world): carts follow corners, slopes and loops at any speed instead of flying off
Powered rails get carts up to speed over a longer stretch, so long lines need more of them
mods.players_install: Yes, to ride carts smoothly on its servers (the client has to move carts the same way); on servers without it, a player's copy switches itself off
guide: Minecarts reach 30 blocks a second, almost 4 times as fast as usual.
They stay on the rails through corners, slopes and loops at full speed.
Use more powered rails than usual: carts take longer to get up to speed.

mods.name: Ahrivaea Woodcutting
mods.summary: The stonecutter cuts wood too: logs into planks, stairs, slabs, fences, doors and more, and into stripped logs, with no crafting grid or sticks.
features: Put any log or wood block in a stonecutter (every wood type, including crimson and warped stems, poplar and bamboo blocks)

One log gives what its 4 planks would make at a crafting table, without needing sticks: 4 planks, 4 stairs, 8 slabs, 2 fences, 1 fence gate, 2 doors, 1 trapdoor, 2 pressure plates, 4 buttons, 2 signs or 8 sticks
Strips logs: log to stripped log, and log or stripped log to (stripped) wood
Planks cut 1:1 like stone: 1 stair, 2 slabs, 1 button or 2 sticks; bamboo planks also make mosaic
Recipes made by tools/woodcutting_recipes.py, plus a tiny bit of code that tells players' games the server has the mod
mods.players_install: No (server only; works for players without the mod)
guide: Put any log or wood block in a stonecutter to make planks, stairs, slabs, fences, doors, signs and more, with no sticks needed.
The stonecutter also strips logs and turns logs into wood.
Planks work too, one at a time, like stone.

mods.name: Ahrivaea Guide
mods.summary: An in-game guide to every Ahrivaea mod: what each one does, how to get started, its commands, and all of its recipes, searchable and filtered by mod.
features: Press G (or type /guide) to open it; the key can be changed in Controls
A tab for every mod with what it adds, how to get started and its commands, and "NEW" on mods you haven't looked at yet; when you join a world, chat says which mods are new
Every recipe from the mods (crafting table, smithing table, stonecutter), filtered by mod or all together, with a search box; ingredients that can be any of a kind (any log) cycle through the options
Hover over an item to see its name and which mod adds it; click it to see every recipe that makes or uses it
Each mod's new items, including ones you don't craft (creature drops)
Built from mods.json and the recipe files every time the mods are built, so it's always up to date
Only shows the mods the server you're on has (in single player, all of them); on a server without any, pressing G says so
guide: Press G any time to open this guide. Pick a mod on the left; About explains it and Recipes shows how to make its items.
Click any item to see what makes it and what it's used in. Type in the search box to find a recipe by name.
Mods marked NEW were added since you last looked.

worlds.name: Ahrivaea (modded world)
worlds.notes: The creature world, reached from the main world by portal

worlds.name: Main world (vanilla)
worlds.notes: Stays fully vanilla (the Gateway is a datapack, which is vanilla)

datapacks.name: Ahrivaea Gateway
datapacks.summary: Portals between the main world and Ahrivaea. The two worlds are separate servers; walking into a portal offers a clickable trip, which moves the player to the other server with Minecraft's own transfer command. A datapack, so the main server stays fully vanilla.
features: /function gateway:build makes a portal 3 blocks in front of you, facing you: a crying obsidian frame around a glowing 3 x 4 opening with portal particles
/function gateway:place turns an opening you built yourself into a portal; /function gateway:remove switches off the nearest one
Step into a portal and chat says where it leads, with a clickable [ Travel there ] (nothing happens by accident); the other server's address is set once with /function gateway:setup
Inventories, XP and spawn points stay separate: each server keeps its own, and players come back to the portal they left from
No messages for 5 seconds after joining, so arriving in a portal doesn't immediately offer the trip back
If a trip can't go through (a server setting missing), the player is told what an operator needs to fix
datapacks.players_install: No (server only, on both servers); players need the Ahrivaea modpack to join Ahrivaea itself
